texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident that occurred on 18.01.2020, in which one Seema Devi (aged about 30) allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 18.01.2020 at 7:30 a.m. victim Seema Devi along with her friends Ruby, Priti, Priyanka, Pinki Devi and their minor children namely Adarsh@Arjun, Kapil, Radhika and Shahil were returning to Delhi from Aligarh after attending a marriage function. All of them were travelling in an Ecco car bearing no.DL-3CCR-1409, which was being driven by one Bhoop Singh. When they reached Chand Hut chowk, Palwal, a truck bearing no.HR-55G-7560 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle), came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco Car. Due to the impact, all the passengers, including the driver, sustained severe injuries. All victims including Seema Devi were rushed to Civil hospital at Palwal and from there she was referred to AIIMS. Her MLC was prepared. 3. An FIR No.0018/2020, dated 18.01.2020, u/s 279/304-A/337 IPC was registered at PS Chand Hut, District Palwal. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/337/338/304A IPC before concerned criminal court. Present claim petition has been filed in respect of grievous injuries to Digitally signed Charu by Charu gupta Date: 2025.12.17 gupta 17:24:14 +0530 MACT No:119/21 Seema Devi vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 2 of 24 BK victim Seema Devi while separate claim petitions were filed before this Tribunal for compensation claim in respect of victim Ruby vide case titled as Ashutosh Dixit vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.225/20, victim Priti vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.123/21, Priyanka vide case titled as Priyanka Devi v. Sant Prakash, MACT no.121/21, minor Adarsh @ Arjun through his mother Priti vide case titled as Adarsh vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.124/21, Usha vide case titled as Usha v. Sant Prakash, MACT no.125/21, minor Gurpreet (since deceased) vide case titled as Priti vs. Sant Prakash, MACT no.118/21, minor Sahil (since deceased) vide case titled as Seema Devi v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.122/21 and Bhoop Singh, vide case titled as Bhoop Singh v. Sant Pakash, MACT no.120/21. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3. In response to the claim petition, respondent no.1 and 2 filed their written statement/reply without denying the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle or allegations or rash and negligent driving. It has been pleaded that Respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle possessed a valid driving licence at the time of accident, that the vehicle was duly insured, that the vehicle was fit to ply on the road and had requisite fitness and permit issued vide Form No.47, NPPUC. 6. A written statement/reply was filed by respondent no.3 denying its liability to compensate the petitioner in case respondent no.1 and 2 were found to be in breach of the terms of the insurance policy. Insurance company has further raised a plea Charu by Charu gupta gupta 2025.12.17 17:24:21 +0530 MACT No:119/21 Seema Devi vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 3 of 24 BK of contributory negligence on the part of victims in as much as the Ecco Car was being plied in violation of the permit, beyond its seating capacity of 7 persons. It is pleaded that the Ecco car admittedly carried 12 passengers including the driver and must have met the accident owing to disbalance. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 19.02.2022. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 18.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-55G-7560 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 8. In order to prove her claim, petitioner/injured examined herself as PW-1. To prove her claim, petitioner /Seema Devi led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein she deposed that on 08.01.2020 at about 7:30 a.m. injured was coming to her home from Aligarh, U.P after attending a marriage function by an Ecco car bearing no.DL3CCR1409 along with Ruby, Priti, Priyanka, Piniki Devi and children namely Arjun, Kapil, Radhika and Shahil. When they reached Chand Hut chowk at village Chandhut Palwal, Haryana, a vehicle bearing no.HR-55G-7560, came from opposite directions in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Ecco car. Due to sudden and forceful impact, injured sustained several grievous injuries. Victim was moved to Civil Hospital, Palwal, Haryana. where doctors referred her to AIIMS Digitally signed by Charu Charu Date: gupta gupta 2025.12.17 17:24:26 +0530 MACT No:119/21 Seema Devi vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 4 of 24 BK Hospital. She was medically examined and her MLC was prepared. PW-1 further deposed that she was doing a private job in New Delhi and earning of Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the injuries, she lost her job. PW-1 was cross examined by all respondents. Ms. Priyanka /PW-2 was examined as an eye witness. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She deposed that she was witness in all the 9 cases and injured in case titled as Priyanka vs. Sant Prakash. She relied upon her Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1, copy of her MLC as Ex.PW1/2, her OPD card as Ex.PW1/3, her medical bills as Ex.PW1/4 and complete criminal record as Ex.PW1/5. She was cross examined by learned counsel for insurance company and the same was adopted by respondent no.1 and 2. 9. Respondents did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. 10. Final arguments in detail were addressed by all the parties.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. However, before such traffic violation can be equated to contributory negligence, the concept of contributory negligence may be analysed through the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramod kumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kungvargi Tak and Ors.,C.A. No.5436 of 1994 decided on 05.08.2002, wherein it has been held as under: "...9. Subject to non-requirement of the existence of duty, the question of contributory negligence is to be decided on the same principle on which the question of defendant's negligence is decided. The standard Charu by Charu gupta gupta 17:24:44 MACT No:119/21 Seema Devi vs.Sant Prakash & ors. P.No. 7 of 24 BK +0530 of reasonable man is as relevant in the case of plaintiff's contributory negligence as in the case of defendant's negligence. But the degree of want of care which will constitute contributory negligence, varies with the circumstances and the factual situation of the case. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi-gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no abso-lute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so , to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of con-tributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiffs share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. Contribu-tory negligence focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. Reliance also placed on recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd. Siddiqui vs. National Insurance Co. (2020) 3SCC 57 wherein the court while considering an issue of triple riding made following observations: " a pillion rider, even if accompanied by more than legally permitted number of passengers, does not automatically imply contributory negligence. For such a finding, it must be demonstrated that the pillion rider's action directly contributed to the occurrence of the accident or exacerbated its impact. The court emphasised that a violation of traffic laws such as exceeding the permissible number of riders on a motorcycle, does not by itself establish contributory negligence. There must be a clear causal connection between the violation and the accident". 16.
